summary: An "ⓘ" button that opens a short explanation on click and keeps it open, so it can hold a link. Not modal, not hover.
useWhen: a field label or a setting needs a sentence of explanation that most people will not need
the explanation links onward — "How retention works" — which a Tooltip cannot hold

useInstead.when: naming an icon-only control, or a hint with nothing to click in it
useInstead.why: a tooltip needs no press to read; a toggletip for a one-word hint makes people click to learn what hovering would have told them

useInstead.when: the content is a task — a form, a choice, anything more than a sentence and a link
useInstead.why: that is a dialog: it takes focus, traps it and has a title; a toggletip is part of the page

useInstead.when: the information is needed to fill the field in
useInstead.why: `description` is always visible; hiding required guidance behind an ⓘ makes people find it by failing first

composition.note: Place it right after the label text it explains. The children are a sentence or two and at most one Link or Button. Name it for its subject — `aria-label="About log retention"`.
composition.example: <>Keep run logs for <Toggletip aria-label="About log retention">Logs past the period are deleted every night. <Link href="/docs/retention">How retention works</Link></Toggletip></>

top.use: the default — above the label, clear of the field below

bottom.use: near the top of the viewport; it also flips here on its own

left.use: beside a label at the end of a row

right.use: beside a label at the start of a row

sm.use: beside body-sm text — field labels, table headers

md.use: beside body text — headings of settings rows

children.note: the explanation; read out on open

a11y.role: button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, controlling a status region
guarantees: opens on click, Enter or Space — never on hover, so it works the same on touch
the bubble follows the button in the DOM, so the next Tab reaches a link inside it
the bubble is a `role="status"` live region that is in the page before it opens, so its text is read out on open while focus stays on the button
Escape closes it and returns focus to the button; inside a Modal, the first Escape closes only the toggletip
a press outside, or focus leaving the button and bubble together, closes it
not modal: no focus trap, nothing on the page hidden from assistive technology
a 24px target at both sizes, pulled into the line so the label is no taller for having one
requires: `aria-label` naming what it explains — "About log retention", not "Info" or "More information"
notes: The bubble is rendered inline, not portalled — that is what keeps it in the Tab order. It is clipped only by an ancestor that is BOTH positioned and clipping (`position` other than static, with `overflow` hidden, auto or scroll): plain `overflow: hidden` does not clip an absolutely positioned descendant whose containing block is higher up. Table's scroll container is exactly that pair, so keep toggletips out of table headers; the demo's smoke test hit-tests the bubble's corners to catch the case.

Inside a <label> or <legend> the button's name becomes part of that label: a RadioGroup reads "Keep run logs for, About log retention". Keep `aria-label` short and led by the subject so the addition informs rather than repeats.

antiPatterns.dont: a Tooltip with a link in it
antiPatterns.why: the tooltip closes as the pointer moves toward the link, and a keyboard user can never reach it

antiPatterns.dont: `aria-label="Info"` on every toggletip on the page
antiPatterns.why: a list of buttons all called "Info" tells a screen reader user nothing about which is which

antiPatterns.dont: a Toggletip holding a form or several actions
antiPatterns.why: focus is not managed into the bubble, so a task inside it is easy to lose

antiPatterns.dont: a Toggletip in a Table header
antiPatterns.why: Table's scroll container is positioned and clips, so the bubble is cut off at the table's edge; explain the column above the table instead
